feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (score 482.7) is the only design that completed any runs: oval 20/20 at 1.69 s mean, s-bend 5/20, slalom 0/20. Its failures were all off-track ends with max_error of 0.060 to 0.064 m, while rms_error stayed at 0.023 to 0.030 m, so the limit is peak excursion on bends. Iteration 2 (score 411.7) changed four things at once (span, track, mass, lead) and the s-bend fell to 0/20, so its cause is not isolated. This package follows your clean test: iteration 1 layout with wheel_track at 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, and 16 mm footprints. I have scaled kp down to 1.4 for the narrower track, because turn rate per unit of turn scales as 1/wheel_track. That cancels most of the extra yaw authority, so if the score barely moves, the track effect is being absorbed by the gain. Integration answers: oscillation at 0.10 m can be read from steering_oscillation on the oval (iteration 1: 0.299). Lead and signal linearity are not separable yet, since iteration 1's signal did not show a lag spike at y = 0.06 m. Next race: if steering_oscillation on the oval stays under about 0.35 and s-bend completion rises above 5/20, keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and try lowering kp further toward 1.2 to see whether the gain was limiting. If s-bend completion does not improve and max_error stays at or above 0.06 m, the track is not the lever, so return to 0.12 m and test the outer sensor weights instead.
requested_changes: If the next race shows s-bend completion above 5/20 with oval steering_oscillation under about 0.35: keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and try kp 1.2 to check whether the gain was limiting. Evidence: iteration 1 (0.12 m track, kp 1.6) finished 5/20 on the s-bend, and iteration 2 (0.10 m, kp 1.4) finished 0/20 when the span was also changed, so the kp effect is not yet isolated.

If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.35 with max_error under 0.06 m: restore wheel_track to 0.12 m and keep the other fields. Evidence: iteration 1 oval steering_oscillation was 0.299 at 0.12 m track, and iteration 2 with the narrower track was 0.291 on the oval at a different span, so the track effect on jitter is still unclear.

If the s-bend stays at 5/20 or fewer and max_error is at or above 0.06 m on the failed runs: return to wheel_track 0.12 m and reduce the outer sensor weights from plus or minus 1.5 to plus or minus 1.0 (inner weights scaled to match). Evidence: iteration 1 failures were all peak excursions at max_error 0.060 to 0.064 m, which points to edge steering gain on bends rather than track width alone.
